# Rich results

*Feature* · also written rich result

Search results with extra visual features, such as ratings, prices or images, that structured data can make a page eligible for.

**Glossary** (*Rich results*): Search results with extra visual features, such as review stars or recipe filters, usually powered by structured data. AI Overviews and AI Mode are not rich results.

Narrative: the topic [Rich results](../topics/rich-results.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

16 claims mention it: 5 from Google's documentation, 10 shown or said at the event (1 not in Google docs, 6 confirmed by Google docs, 3 consistent with Google docs), 1 the author's analysis. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Structured data markup that Google Search supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/search-gallery), [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery).

- [`D1-C265`](../sessions/D1-S04-lightning-session-a-automation-and-ai.md) Docs: Search Console Help separates critical issues, which make a structured-data item invalid and stop it from appearing as a rich result, from non-critical issues, listed under 'Improve item appearance'; the Rich Results Test reports valid items that have warnings. `[D1-C265, docs, Google Search Console Help, https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7552505?hl=en]`
- [`D2-C480`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Docs: Google's guide to optimizing for generative AI features lists 'overfocusing on structured data' among the things site owners don't need to do: structured data is not required for generative AI search and no special schema.org markup is needed, though it remains worth using because it helps pages become eligible for rich results. `[D2-C480, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/ai-optimization-guide]`
- [`D2-C501`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Docs: Google's general structured data guidelines say a structured data manual action removes a page's eligibility for rich results but does not affect how the page ranks in web search. `[D2-C501, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/sd-policies]`
- [`D2-C834`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Docs: Google's merchant listing guide says Product rich results only support pages that focus on a single product, or on several variants of the same product. `[D2-C834, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing]`
- [`D3-C315`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Docs: Google's Visual Elements gallery describes a text result as based on the page's textual content, with attribution, title link and snippet; attribution can include the site name, favicon and visible URL, and a rich result typically relies on structured data. `[D3-C315, docs, Google Search Central, https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery]`

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D1-C122`](../sessions/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) Stage, Day 1, not in Google docs: Check and focus on rich results for Google. `[D1-C122, stage, a speaker, Day 1]`
- [`D2-C498`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Slide, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google recommends testing and previewing structured data in the Rich Results Test, which shows the rich result features it detected and whether the markup is valid. `[D2-C498, slide, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C324`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Rich results differ from other search features because Google builds them from extra data that site owners provide, usually structured data and usually in JSON-LD format. `[D3-C324, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C325`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: AI Mode and AI Overviews are not rich results but standard search features: they need no structured data to function and work with the normal text results from Google's index. `[D3-C325, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C333`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Slide, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google's Article rich results slide said structured data can be used to indicate that content is behind a paywall. `[D3-C333, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C335`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google described the site name as an attribution feature rather than a rich result, and said site owners can influence which site name Google shows for their site in search results. `[D3-C335, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C343`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, confirmed by Google docs: Google Search displays product rich results from product structured data; it may also use the product data a merchant provides in Google Merchant Center, but Merchant Center is not required for them. `[D3-C343, stage, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D2-C521`](../sessions/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Structured data makes pages eligible to appear as rich results, Google's structured data talk said in its recap. `[D2-C521, stage, Google, Day 2]`
- [`D3-C331`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Slide, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google's rich results slide said Article structured data is not required to appear in Top Stories but is highly recommended for all articles. `[D3-C331, slide, Google, Day 3]`
- [`D3-C342`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Stage, Day 3, consistent with Google docs: Google called product rich results essential for any e-commerce business; they can show the product's rating, the number of reviews and other details. `[D3-C342, stage, Google, Day 3]`

## The author's analysis

- [`D3-C351`](../sessions/D3-S10-how-search-results-are-born.md) Analysis: For an online shop, Product structured data is enough for product rich results and Google Images product annotations, but the Shopping tab needs a Merchant Center feed too; keep feed and markup values identical, since Google can use the markup to validate the feed. `[D3-C351, analysis, Ibrahim Anjro]`

## For developers

- `DEV-AIF-02` **SHOULD** · Documented: Spend no effort on llms.txt, AI text files or AI-specific markup for Google (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SDA-02` **MUST** · Documented: Mark up only content that is visible on the page and relevant to it (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SDA-07` **SHOULD** · Documented: Describe only the page's main product in Product markup, not related-product carousels (1 of its claims mentions it; its own text names it)
- `DEV-SDA-11` **MUST** · Documented: Validate markup in the Rich Results Test before it reaches templates, and monitor it after release (2 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-SDA-13` **SHOULD** · Documented: Add Article markup with headline, images, dates and authors to every article template (2 of its claims mention it)
- `DEV-SDA-15` **SHOULD** · Documented: State the preferred site name with WebSite markup on the home page (1 of its claims mentions it)
- `DEV-SHP-01` **SHOULD** · Documented: Use Product markup for rich results and a Merchant Center feed for the Shopping tab, with identical values (2 of its claims mention it; its own text names it)
